_meta.purpose: Executable ground truth for public_benchmarks.bots.ingest_adapter, mirrored from URGENCY_TO_SEVERITY in that module so the mapping is auditable outside Python.
_meta.source_dataset: Splunk BOTS (any version -- the notable-event schema this adapter targets is version-independent)
_meta.not_verified_against: an actual downloaded Splunk BOTS export (unavailable in this development environment) -- verified only against hand-built schema-conformant sample rows in tests/test_phase83_public_benchmarks_bots.py

unrecognized_or_missing_urgency_default.surfaced_as: ConvertReport.unrecognized_urgency -- never silently absorbed or guessed

native_id_strategy: prefers the event's own event_id/_cd if the export carries one; otherwise a deterministic hash of the row content plus its position, so re-running the adapter on the same export is reproducible

usable_directly: anomaly (alert rate / severity distribution over time)
peer_benchmark (alert volume/severity vs. a peer cohort of other converted BOTS windows)
coverage_gap / detection_gap (assets with zero alerts vs. assets with notable events)
requires_workflow_augmentation: execution_gap (needs acknowledged_at/closed_at -- a raw notable event has neither unless the export also includes Splunk ES's incident-review workflow fields, which this adapter does not currently read)
negative_space (needs cases/escalations/dispositions -- a raw notable event export has none)
